title: Deviations, Incomplete Work and Honest Status

content.overview: Cultivation work can deviate from plan. Technicians must preserve factual status, record incomplete work honestly and hand unresolved conditions forward without inventing data or completion.

vocabulary.definition: A documented departure from an approved instruction, expected condition, specification or planned process.
A condition anticipated by a procedure that requires a defined alternate action or approval.
Accurately representing what was done, what was not done and what remains unresolved.

sections.title: Deviations are operational information
sections.body: Equipment faults, identity mismatches, alarms, material shortages, contamination concerns and other conditions can interrupt work. The technician preserves what actually happened rather than forcing the record to appear normal.

sections.title: Never manufacture completion
sections.body: A task is complete only when required steps and acceptance criteria are met or an authorized exception is documented. Missed observations remain missing; they are not reconstructed from guesses or memory and presented as contemporaneous data.

workedExamples: An interrupted sanitation cycle is documented as incomplete instead of being signed complete.
A missed measurement is recorded according to the missing-data procedure rather than invented later.
commonMistakes: Hiding deviations because they feel like personal failure.
Marking work complete simply because the shift ended.
content.practicalApplication: Review a partially completed work packet, identify deviations and incomplete steps, decide what can continue or must stop, and write the handoff status.
content.summary: Reliable operations depend on truthful status. Technicians document deviations and incomplete work as they occurred and make unresolved conditions visible.
